pull_request.title: Calorimeter: common HCAL readout baseline design
pull_request.head: codex/hcal-realism-assessment
pull_request.body:
## Executive summary

Introduce a reusable HCAL tile/readout module for the human-directed 14 TeV hadron-collider study. Two identical 36-tile boards share a carrier, cooling and service interface, with explicit physical gaps, channel ownership, material and continuous-power budgets.

The paired unit is 3.018 kg and 5.939 W under the stated planning assumptions. The DAQ screen uses 93.75% of assumed capacity at 750 kHz and exposes overload at 1 MHz. Review of those operating and physical choices is the next decision; this remains an isolated DRAFT/PROTOTYPE.

## Change

- Add DES035's ODD HCAL technology/realism assessment and staged prototype programme, followed by the DES036 common-module design, schematic and source catalogue.
- Add a deterministic, standalone DD4hep fixture: scintillator host, SiPM/LED package proxies, PCB/front-end envelopes, shared cold plate and actual cooling bores, service boundaries, stable tile IDs and separate DAQ/trigger budgets.
- Allocate one H2GCROC-class chip per board: 36 connected ordinary inputs, 36 unused ordinary inputs and six auxiliary channels; budget all 78 channels continuously.
- Add negative controls, native shape/material/placement/navigation checks and saved-event transport checks bound to executed inputs and output hashes. Independent PhysVal findings were corrected and reviewed at `97d0bb64c22f63c0680c543a97c5b05ce2acc4b8`.

Governing documents: [DES035](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/b22b75bc1b67af799d921d3a5c42756948b54854/docs/design/DES-035-hcal-realism-and-prototype-plan.md), [DES036](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/b22b75bc1b67af799d921d3a5c42756948b54854/docs/design/DES-036-hcal-common-readout-module.md). Tracking: `TASK-B-HCAL-REALISM`, `TASK-B-HCAL-COMMON-MODULE`.

## Dashboard and validation

- [x] Update project tracking with scope, deliverables and exact review/evidence revisions.
- [x] Run relevant controls and session/project/token validators; retain actual results and limitations.
- [x] Preserve human approval boundaries: collision energy is confirmed; other operating inputs remain explicit project planning choices.
- [x] Layout main page/R–Z unaffected: standalone fixture only; no production detector or repeated assembly integration.

Executed evidence at `97d0bb6`: 44 module/provenance controls, 14 existing calorimeter regressions; native factory build and audit of 395 physical parts, 72 unique sensitive IDs, 360 cell probes and zero reported overlaps at 1e-5 mm; two saved Geant4 muon events with finite positive-energy hits. Runtime identities, hashes and scope are retained in the [validation report](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/b22b75bc1b67af799d921d3a5c42756948b54854/docs/validation/DES-036/results.md).

No optical-response, radiation, sustained-rate, manufacturing or thermal/hydraulic qualification is claimed. Luminosity/pileup and regional lifetime radiation/temperature targets remain open. The smoke uses gun argument `10*GeV`; saved primary momentum is independently checked as 10 GeV/c. Seed/physics settings are verified against recorded execution metadata.


## Calorimeter baseline campaign — 2026-11-04

Ordinary integration merges preserve current main, original source histories and canonical accounting. The common module is shared; regional configurations remain Si–W baseline design options. LAr regional reparameterization and replay, native full HCAL assemblies, connected services and response/engineering qualification remain follow-ups.

ECAL replacement: [PR115](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/115). Provenance/accounting: [PR116](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/116). Stable tasks: `TASK-B-HCAL-REALISM, TASK-B-HCAL-COMMON-MODULE`.

Realism owner15,407,135; common-module owner31,154,394; publication owner2,886,448 observed tokens. These retain separate canonical owners. Shared campaign accounts are references, not per-PR cost allocations. Current coordinator root usage remains active and excluded. Exact ownership, observed input/output counters, visible interactions and limitations are retained in canonical journals/individual ledgers.

Merge queue:116 →115 →81 →84/85. Open campaign PRs target main, so after each dependency lands the next diff shrinks against main; do not merge into an already-merged parent branch. No design lifecycle is advanced or engineering approval inferred.

## Executive summary

Introduce a reusable HCAL tile/readout module for the human-directed 14 TeV hadron-collider study. Two identical 36-tile boards share a carrier, cooling and service interface, with explicit physical gaps, channel ownership, material and continuous-power budgets.

The paired unit is 3.018 kg and 5.939 W under the stated planning assumptions. The DAQ screen uses 93.75% of assumed capacity at 750 kHz and exposes overload at 1 MHz. Review of those operating and physical choices is the next decision; this remains an isolated DRAFT/PROTOTYPE.

## Change

- Add DES035's ODD HCAL technology/realism assessment and staged prototype programme, followed by the DES036 common-module design, schematic and source catalogue.
- Add a deterministic, standalone DD4hep fixture: scintillator host, SiPM/LED package proxies, PCB/front-end envelopes, shared cold plate and actual cooling bores, service boundaries, stable tile IDs and separate DAQ/trigger budgets.
- Allocate one H2GCROC-class chip per board: 36 connected ordinary inputs, 36 unused ordinary inputs and six auxiliary channels; budget all 78 channels continuously.
- Add negative controls, native shape/material/placement/navigation checks and saved-event transport checks bound to executed inputs and output hashes. Independent PhysVal findings were corrected and reviewed at `97d0bb64c22f63c0680c543a97c5b05ce2acc4b8`.

Governing documents: [DES035](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/b22b75bc1b67af799d921d3a5c42756948b54854/docs/design/DES-035-hcal-realism-and-prototype-plan.md), [DES036](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/b22b75bc1b67af799d921d3a5c42756948b54854/docs/design/DES-036-hcal-common-readout-module.md). Tracking: `TASK-B-HCAL-REALISM`, `TASK-B-HCAL-COMMON-MODULE`.

## Dashboard and validation

- [x] Update project tracking with scope, deliverables and exact review/evidence revisions.
- [x] Run relevant controls and session/project/token validators; retain actual results and limitations.
- [x] Preserve human approval boundaries: collision energy is confirmed; other operating inputs remain explicit project planning choices.
- [x] Layout main page/R–Z unaffected: standalone fixture only; no production detector or repeated assembly integration.

Executed evidence at `97d0bb6`: 44 module/provenance controls, 14 existing calorimeter regressions; native factory build and audit of 395 physical parts, 72 unique sensitive IDs, 360 cell probes and zero reported overlaps at 1e-5 mm; two saved Geant4 muon events with finite positive-energy hits. Runtime identities, hashes and scope are retained in the [validation report](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/b22b75bc1b67af799d921d3a5c42756948b54854/docs/validation/DES-036/results.md).

No optical-response, radiation, sustained-rate, manufacturing or thermal/hydraulic qualification is claimed. Luminosity/pileup and regional lifetime radiation/temperature targets remain open. The smoke uses gun argument `10*GeV`; saved primary momentum is independently checked as 10 GeV/c. Seed/physics settings are verified against recorded execution metadata.


## Calorimeter baseline campaign — 2026-11-04

Ordinary integration merges preserve current main, original source histories and canonical accounting. The common module is shared; regional configurations remain Si–W baseline design options. LAr regional reparameterization and replay, native full HCAL assemblies, connected services and response/engineering qualification remain follow-ups.

ECAL replacement: [PR115](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/115). Provenance/accounting: [PR116](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/116). Stable tasks: `TASK-B-HCAL-REALISM, TASK-B-HCAL-COMMON-MODULE`.

Realism owner15,407,135; common-module owner31,154,394; publication owner2,886,448 observed tokens. These retain separate canonical owners. Shared campaign accounts are references, not per-PR cost allocations. Current coordinator root usage remains active and excluded. Exact ownership, observed input/output counters, visible interactions and limitations are retained in canonical journals/individual ledgers.

Merge queue:116 →115 →81 →84/85. Open campaign PRs target main, so after each dependency lands the next diff shrinks against main; do not merge into an already-merged parent branch. No design lifecycle is advanced or engineering approval inferred.

Exact user direction: “Ok, let's assume this is the common readout module - can
you go on and design a Barrel and Endcap HCAL accordingly (separate PRs) please”.
This task develops the barrel proposal; the companion region has a separate
worktree/PR and journal. Both start from clean common-module head
`abd95bdc64b9d7971561d659bf953e71de4e7e99`, PR81. The human selected a working
basis at14TeV, not engineering sign-off. ParentPR81 remained OPEN/draft with
hosted build and token-site SUCCESS when checked. Proposals are sibling branches
against its head branch, so neither regional diff includes the other.

Read AGENTS/PROJECT and applicable design/ADR/layout/role instructions. Applied
nodd-coordinate, nodd-design-evidence and nodd-review-validation. Explicit
role-prompt fallback was used, with complete prepared prompts; native profile
loading was not verified. No production detector changes or dependency installs.
Exact start/client identity/per-turn usage were not exposed.

**Steel–scintillator is an appropriate HCAL baseline for a hadron collider. The main gaps are in the readout, radiation qualification, material accounting, coverage and system integration.**

I saved the detailed investigation, sources and staged plan in [DES035 — HCAL realism assessment]([redacted]

**Technology suitability.** ATLAS Tile demonstrates steel–scintillator calorimetry in sustained pp operation. Its fibre/PMT readout differs from ODD’s implied granular tile architecture, so its performance cannot simply be transferred. CMS HGCAL provides a relevant SiPM-on-tile precedent, with sensor technology chosen according to regional radiation exposure. [ATLAS operating experience](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.16034v2), [CMS tile-readout validation]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).

CALICE is a strong mechanical and active-element precedent, but its particular electronics need reconsideration for pp operation. SPIROC2E stores signals in 16 analog-memory cells and alternates acquisition with digitization/readout. Continuous cooling alone cannot establish the required rate capability, buffering or trigger behavior. Modern H2GCROC-class electronics illustrate the functions a suitable architecture must provide. [CALICE prototype](https://arxiv.org/html/2209.15327v1), [HGCROC/H2GCROC production study]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).

My recommendation is to retain steel–scintillator centrally, while keeping the most exposed endcap and forward regions conditional on dose, fluence, occupancy and end-of-life signal-to-noise studies.

**The largest modeling issue is the effective electronics material.** Current upstream ODD repeats this stack 36 times:

| Component | Per layer |
|---|---:|
| Steel235 | 30 mm |
| Copper-rich `siPCBMix` | 16 mm |
| Sensitive scintillator | 3 mm |
| Air, labelled services | 2 mm |
| **Total** | **51 mm** |

That gives a 1.836 m stack. The scintillator consists of continuous sensitive sheets divided into logical 30 mm cells; individual tiles, wrapping, SiPMs and board boundaries are absent. I verified that the current upstream HCAL, material, envelope and factory files match the earlier audited source hashes. The 16 mm mixture needs its original physical rationale established. Across the stack, it contains **238.2 g/cm² of copper**, equivalent to approximately **266 mm of solid copper**. That copper alone contributes roughly **1.73 nuclear interaction lengths**, using PDG data. Replacing it with realistic electronics therefore changes containment and sampling response substantially—even when all steel plates remain. It should neither be silently corrected to 1.6 mm nor removed as harmless packaging. [PDG copper properties](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/AtomicNuclearProperties/HTML/copper_Cu.html).

**The existing nODD prototypes already address several physical omissions**, but their limitations matter:

| Area | Present progress | Remaining feasibility gap |
|---|---|---|
| Tile assemblies | DES028 adds physical tiles, reflectors, SiPM packages, boards and cooling | Optical coupling, manufactured scintillator, irradiation behavior and actual electronics remain hypotheses |
| Readout | Explicit package/channel and power inventories | Continuous acquisition, dynamic range, latency, bandwidth and radiation tolerance are unselected |
| Coverage | DES029 constructs complete isolated assemblies | HCAL active face fractions are only 52.9–78.3% in barrel layers and 38.8% in endcaps |

| Physics response | Native geometry checks and sparse muon transport exist | Hadron showers, digitization, pileup, aging, jets and missing-momentum tails remain unvalidated |

The older detailed assembly and the **current enlarged HCAL outline are different configurations**. Its previous mass, cooling totals and overlap results cannot be applied to the new outline. Likewise, the external service study budgets ECAL services; it has not demonstrated capacity for HCAL services.

Forward coverage also needs separate work: η = 4 rays remain inside the current HCAL aperture. The empty FCal reservation does not establish the intended calorimetry reach toward η = 5.

**The proposed development sequence follows the ECAL prototype method:**

1. **Define the operating contract.** Preserve the existing 14 TeV study direction; specify bunch structure, pileup, lifetime exposure, regional radiation maps, energy range and acceptance criteria.

2. **Develop one representative continuous-readout tile module.** Select a documented scintillator, reflector, SiPM and front-end concept. Establish beginning- and end-of-life light yield, noise, saturation, timing, power and calibration requirements.

3. **Build a serviced barrel carrier and an inner endcap carrier.** Follow the ECAL’s compact-board hierarchy, shared interfaces and explicit boundary components. Use manufacturable edge tiles and board families; repair the large inner holes before relying on staggering.

4. **Reassess absorber depth and sector geometry.** Compare the original copper-rich stack with the physical replacement using native interaction-length maps and hadron leakage distributions. Additional steel, layers or a tail catcher should follow those requirements.

5. **Regenerate the full HCAL inside the selected layout.** Recalculate channels, mass, heat, cooling and bandwidth. Demonstrate connected services, support loads, magnetic compatibility, installation access and barrel/endcap/FCal transitions.

6. **Validate response and reconstructed performance.** Add sourced quenching, light collection, SiPM and electronics response; test hadrons across energies and cracks, then in-time/out-of-time pileup, jets and missing-momentum tails. Geometry, digitization and reconstruction changes should be compared separately.

The immediate useful deliverable is **the operating contract plus one realistic readout module and serviced carrier**. Full repetition should follow their evidence.

The investigation passed **28 existing controls**, source/hash and arithmetic checks, and repository-record validation. No new shower simulation or engineering qualification was performed; DES035 remains a draft proposal for human review.

**Conclusion — INFERENCE:** steel/scintillator remains a credible HCAL technology for a hadron collider, especially centrally. The present evidence does **not** qualify a warm, uniformly instrumented CALICE-like SiPM-on-tile calorimeter across the whole barrel/endcap. ### Verified public evidence and catalogue-ready metadata

All sources accessed **2026-10-15**. No new local reference copies or hashes were created.

1. **Existing `SRC-CALICE-AHCAL-2022`:** CALICE Collaboration, *Design, Construction and Commissioning of a Technological Prototype of a Highly Granular SiPM-on-tile Scintillator-Steel Hadronic Calorimeter*, **arXiv:2209.15327v1, 2022-09-30**. Actual primary HTML inspected:  
   [Versioned paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2209.15327v1).

   **FACT:** §§2.1–2.2 describe 360 × 360 mm HBUs, 144 directly coupled SiPM/tile channels, 3 mm scintillator and 30 mm tile pitch; §2.7 describes 6.4 mm cassettes including two 0.5 mm steel covers. §§2.3–2.3.1 explicitly describe acquisition followed by digitization/readout, 16-cell analog memory, BUSY stopping acquisition, selectable 250 kHz–5 MHz bunch clock, and ILC power pulsing. The distributed 40 MHz clock is divided down by the DIF (§2.3.2). §2.8 cools interface boards; active-layer cooling is omitted because of pulsed low consumption. 2. **Suggested `SRC-ATLAS-TILE-RUN2-2025`:** ATLAS Collaboration, *Operation and performance of the ATLAS tile calorimeter in LHC Run 2*, **arXiv:2401.16034v2, 2025-01-10**; CERN-EP-2023-266; *Eur. Phys. J. C* **84 (2024) 1313**; DOI **10.1140/epjc/s10052-024-13151-4**.

[PDG composition/density rows](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/AtomicNuclearProperties/HTML/polystyrene.html).

**NODD DESIGN CHOICE:** name a new **undoped-polystyrene bulk proxy**, C8H8 at 1.060 g/cm³, for the module study. It is not a fully specified scintillator formulation. Retaining 1.032 g/cm³ instead remains a separate density choice, rather than a PDG fact. Preserve DES028’s C19H21 material unchanged as the historical control. Do not infer scintillation yield, quenching, radiation durability or optical transport from the new stoichiometry.

### Concrete mechanical fixture

All dimensions below are **proposed NODD DESIGN CHOICES**, with no human sign-off:

- Common board: **182 × 182 × 1.2 mm**, with explicit **0.07 mm equivalent Cu** and remaining G10 proxy.
- Tiles: **6 × 6 on 30 mm pitch**, **29.7 × 29.7 × 3 mm** core. The tile normal, row/column and connector-facing board edge are explicit.
- Reflector: retain **0.1 mm effective PET shell** as a named bulk approximation; it is not the actual ESR optical/material construction.
- Dimple: retain a simple **2.5 mm radius**, changeable **1.1 mm depth effective cavity**, to accommodate the reference SiPM mounting allocation. This cylindrical cavity does not claim a proven optical profile.
- ASIC: **25 × 25 × 2 mm project allocation**, centred on the board’s rear face, with 0.1 mm attachment and 0.2 mm thermal interface. **Actual H2GCROC die/package/land-pattern dimensions remain unverified.** No public package drawing found in the examined sources justifies reusing DES028’s 10 × 10 mm package.
- Reserve discrete LED, temperature-monitor, passive/regulator and connector envelopes. Their bulk materials/counts are explicit; LED optical injection and the actual supporting circuits remain unresolved.
- Two boards: **0.5 mm board-to-board gap**, giving a **364.5 mm combined PCB span**.
- Shared carrier fixture: **372 × 210 × 11.5 mm**, with a peripheral **20 mm interface bay** and named mechanical margins. Endcap carriers may use fewer boards; the common board does not determine global carrier shape.
- Shared cold plate: **3 mm aluminium**, with channels cut for **2 mm OD/1.6 mm ID Ti tubes**, represented as complementary plate/pipe/coolant volumes. This gives finite enclosing thermal contact rather than relying on a tangent tube touching a plate.
- **One shared interface and cooling assembly**, not a full duplicate cassette around each common board. The absorber remains sector owned; only a standalone fixture adds one **30 mm plate patch**.

A consistent example in the local depth coordinate is:

| Depth [mm] | Part |
|---|---|
| 0–0.5 | Front stainless proxy cover |
| 0.5–0.7 | Clearance |
| 0.7–3.9 | Wrapped tile envelope |
| 3.9–4.0 | Adhesive/contact region |
| 4.0–5.2 | PCB |
| 5.2–5.3 | ASIC attachment |
| 5.3–7.3 | ASIC package allocation |
| 7.3–7.5 | Thermal pad |
| 7.5–10.5 | Shared cooled plate, with pipe/coolant subtraction |
| 10.5–10.625 | Electrical insulation |
| 10.625–11.0 | Clearance |
| 11.0–11.5 | Rear cover |

The SiPM occupies a pierced reflector/dimple region on the PCB’s tile side. Do not fill the same volume with package, reflector, adhesive and scintillator. Tile adhesive should use explicit dots or a normalized effective coverage, not a full overlapping sheet.

This stack demonstrates an internally consistent allocation. Thermal contact resistance, board conduction to cool SiPMs, mounting stiffness, tube joining, tolerances and leak/condensation protection remain unqualified.

### Power and service fixture

**NODD DESIGN CHOICE:** budget **15 mW for each of all 78 internal channels**, hence **1.17 W/ASIC**. This is conservative project accounting anchored to the published requirement, not a measured worst-case part specification. Keep ASIC heat independent of connected tile count.

For the paired carrier, an illustrative ledger uses:

- ASICs: **2.34 W**.
- Shared interface allowance: **2 W/carrier**, explicitly a new budgeting hypothesis.
- Conversion efficiency: **90%**.
- SiPM bias: representative **42 V** and **2 µA/tile** beginning-of-life hypothesis.
- Total: **4.82827 W/carrier**.
- Ideal water flow at **5 K** rise, Cp = 4,180 J/(kg K): **0.23102 g/s**.

All are **INFERENCE from prototype choices**. Recalculate for operating bias by device, irradiated dark current, supporting circuits and temperature. A 12 V carrier input requires explicit conversion to the actual electronics rails; it is not the ASIC supply specification.

Carrier ports should identify supply/return, LV/return, bias/return, fast clock/control, slow control and per-chip data/trigger links. Place shared concentration at the carrier bay; record ownership of its heat and materials. A port graph must terminate at a named next-stage handoff.

### Comparison and completion gates

The square board offers a smaller reusable unit for inner/edge packing. Compared with one 6 × 12 board for the same 72 tiles, it doubles ASIC inventory and conservatively allocated chip power; the hardware comparison must show that cost openly. Sharing one ASIC between two square boards is a later alternative requiring analog interconnect/capacitance/noise and connector evidence.

Before scaling, require:

1. Independent dimensions/counts/constituent masses; native overlap and sensitive ID checks.
2. Exact accounting of 36 connected, 36 unused ordinary and six auxiliary channels per chip.
3. Negative controls for extra tiles, auxiliary misuse, duplicate absorber, overlapping cavity constituents and blocked/disconnected ports.
4. Separate maps of tile, PCB, seam, carrier and service areas.
5. Response, power, thermal and irradiation assumptions visibly conditional.

Actual checks were pinned-source inspection, primary public text/PDF inspection, and independent read-only channel/power/flow arithmetic. **14 TeV alone selects neither the readout package nor the SiPM irradiation qualification, operating temperature or regional deployment.**

**HCALASSEMBLY-20261015-CaloTech completed read-only** at **`abd95bdc64b9d7971561d659bf953e71de4e7e99`**. No files changed, delegation, runtime activation or publication. The six assigned inputs were inspected; DES035 is unchanged from the previously examined blob.

**Recommendation — proposed NODD DESIGN CHOICE:** start the endcap with full-face Cartesian packing grouped into four mechanical quadrants, using the **unchanged DES036 380 × 240 × 12 mm paired carrier and 184 mm common boards**. Keep a uniform-grid control and explicitly evaluate an aperture-adaptive inner-row arrangement. Avoid making sixteen narrow wedges the module-packing boundaries.

### Depth and boundary contract

**FACT — pinned DES034/LAYOUT001:** front |z| = **4,883.2 mm**, back |z| = **6,379.1 mm**, inner apothem **300 mm**, outer apothem **4,085.9 mm**. DES036 has a **12 mm carrier**.

**INFERENCE:** even zero installation gap gives `36 × (30 + 12) = 1,512 mm`, exceeding the old **1,495.9 mm** complete depth before a back cover. Do not compress the carrier or silently remove steel/layers.

Following the coordinator’s subsequent explicit amendment proposal:

- Preserve **36 layers**, **30 mm sector-owned steel**, **12 mm carrier**, **1 mm installation gap**.
- Use **43 mm repeat pitch** and **10 mm back cover**.
- Total depth: **1,558 mm**; revised back **|z| = 6,441.2 mm**.
- Revised outer endcap apothem **4,148 mm**, following the companion barrel proposal.
- Retain front **4,883.2 mm** and inner apothem **300 mm**.
- Retain the FCal reservation **R = 80–290 mm, |z| = 4,533.2–6,379.1 mm** unchanged.

These are proposed envelope amendments, not facts about the pinned outline. The FCal reservation ends before the revised HCAL rear; this does not authorize extending it or establish a forward shower-depth handover.

An explicit layer convention is:

`steel [z_l,z_l+30] → carrier [z_l+30,z_l+42] → installation gap [z_l+42,z_l+43]`

with `z_l = 4883.2 + 43l`, `l = 0…35`. DES036 scintillator cores occupy carrier-local z = **0.5–3.5 mm**.

### Quantified packing comparison

**FACT — DES036/config:** one carrier owns 72 tiles, with board centres **(−93,−12), (+93,−12) mm**. Tile centres within each board are spaced by 30 mm; cores are 29.7 mm square.

**INFERENCE:** intrinsic projected core area is

`72 × 29.7² / (380 × 240) = 69.6387%`.

Thus unchanged paired carriers cannot deliver 90% face coverage, even with perfect footprint packing. This is a projected active-face fraction, not detection efficiency.

I ran an independent, dependency-free analytic screen using:

- Revised outer apothem **4,148 mm**;
- **20 mm outer rim** reservation;
- **10 mm inner-aperture clearance**, implemented by an excluded 16-gon of apothem 310 mm;
- Exact outer-polygon corner containment;
- Rectangle–inner-polygon separating-axis rejection;
- No clipped carrier, board or tile.

The denominator is the complete original-aperture annular face, **54.4730 m²**, including the rim reservation.

| Illustrative layout | Carriers/layer | Projected core fraction |
|---|---:|---:|
| Quadrants; 1 mm row gaps; 20 mm full quadrant seams | 524 | 61.09% |
| **Quadrants; 20 mm row collector strips; 20 mm full quadrant seams** | **484** | **56.43%** |
| Simple 16-wedge rows, 380 mm carrier dimension tangent | 336 | 39.17% |
| Simple 16-wedge rows, rotated 240 mm dimension tangent | 432 | 50.37% |

These are reproducible candidate packings, not optimized or native-validated designs. The rotated-wedge count is particularly sensitive to whether the last radial row fits.

For the proposed quadrant control, carrier centres are

`x = ±(200 + 381i) mm`, `y = ±(130 + 260j) mm`, `i,j ≥ 0`,

followed by the polygon/aperture acceptance tests. This gives 20 mm full seams on the axes, 1 mm between columns and 20 mm between rows. Each quadrant has 121 accepted carriers.

For a narrow wedge with half-angle α = π/16, tangent width W and edge allowance e, the necessary inner-edge condition is

`r_inner ≥ (W/2 + e) / tan(α)`.

With e = 21 mm, it gives **1,060.77 mm** for W = 380 mm and **708.85 mm** for W = 240 mm. Even the unchanged **184 mm board** cannot fit at the 300 mm aperture inside such a narrow wedge: the unallocated wedge width there is only **119.35 mm**.

### Inner coverage: remaining limitation and next comparison

The uniform quadrant control has first projected tile core at approximately **r = 399.14 mm**. This is a consequence of the chosen row origins, **not an unavoidable minimum of the unchanged carrier**.

For example, an unchanged carrier centred at **(0,430) mm** is tangent to the expanded 310 mm aperture and reaches approximately **r = 328.17 mm** active radius, but crosses the quadrant seam. A carrier at **(200,430) mm** remains within the positive quadrant and reaches approximately **328.60 mm**. It conflicts with the uniform following row at y = 650 mm, so its column’s subsequent row origins must change.

**Proposed priority:** compare aperture-adaptive row origins using the same carrier before commissioning custom boards or tiles. Keep all board/carrier envelopes intact, check neighbours globally, and retain the uniform control. If the resulting staircase boundary still fails the required directional sampling, propose a distinct inner carrier using unchanged common boards; do not call that carrier redesign “module standardization.”

I also evaluated the actual individual tile-core mask at **720 uniformly spaced φ samples**, using the 36 active-plane midpoints. For the quadrant control:

| |η| | Aligned planes: minimum/mean/maximum active planes | Four-layer 0°,22.5°,45°,67.5° pattern |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2.0 | 0 / 23.383 / 35 | 13 / 23.383 / 30 |
| 2.5 | 0 / 23.061 / 36 | 14 / 23.061 / 31 |
| 3.0 | 0 / 15.858 / 35 | 5 / 15.858 / 30 |
| 3.2 | 0 / 7.633 / 36 | 0 / 7.633 / 20 |
| 3.4 | 0 / 1.194 / 11 | 0 / 1.194 / 5 |
| 3.5, 4.0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

At |η| = 3.2 and 3.4, the staggered example still gives zero active planes for approximately **26.4%** and **53.1%** of sampled φ, respectively. Therefore it cannot support a blanket acceptance claim.

These are analytic plane-mask diagnostics, not finite-volume transport. A 90° pattern preserves quadrant-axis cracks; the 22.5° pattern can move them because the outer 16-gon has that rotational symmetry. Its supports, row collectors and connections would also have to follow the layer orientation. Staggering is conditional on a mechanically coherent implementation.

### Counts, services and ownership

For the 484-carrier/layer control over 36 layers and both endcaps:

- **34,848 carriers**, **69,696 common boards**;
- **2,509,056 physical tiles/SiPMs**;
- **5,436,288 budgeted powered internal channels**;
- **139,392 local cooling handoff endpoints**;
- Approximately **206.98 kW nominal local heat** and **9.90 kg/s ideal water** at 5 K rise, using the unchanged DES036 hypotheses.

New collectors, trunks, concentrators, regulation losses and external cooling loads are additional. Do not use the pre-existing ECAL route budget as spare HCAL capacity.

The 20 mm row strips should own explicit collector/data paths connected to the DES036 face handoffs. They are not automatically functional manifolds. Route along rows to a named outer-rim collector, then to the approved system handoff. Account for discontinuous rows near the bore/polygon edges, bend/access space, connections, hydraulic losses, LV drop, concentration bandwidth and fault domains. The existing 93.75%/125% DES036 DAQ scenarios remain conditional after aggregation.

Separate ownership:

- **Module:** unchanged tiles, SiPM/LED envelopes, PCB, front-end allocation and local thermal contact.
- **Carrier:** existing covers/plate/tubes/interface and local handoffs.
- **Layer/quadrant:** absorber pieces, carrier attachment, row collectors and support frame.
- **System:** endcap global support, external manifolds/trunks, ECAL/FCal and barrel-gap interfaces.

Keep absorber steel present underneath the row corridors unless a separately recorded penetration changes it; avoid accidentally turning carrier setbacks into missing absorber.

Use stable composite IDs `(system, side, layer, carrier, module, tile)` with layer **0–35**, module **0–1**, tile **0–35** and explicitly bounded carrier indices. Quadrant or angular bookkeeping need not dictate mechanical sector boundaries. The negative endcap requires a proper rotation and corresponding local outward-z convention.

The next implementation should publish complete masks, minimum/mean/quantiles of active-layer count, first/last active layer and material depth versus η/φ, with dense seam/aperture sampling. Counts and material totals must reproduce the accepted placements before native construction and transport checks.

**Source locators:** DES036 §§“Common board,” “Shared carrier,” “Material and service ledger”; DES029 repair §§“Where the reported area goes,” “Recommended design sequence”; DES034 §§“External backbone,” “Forward reservation”; LAYOUT001 `hcal`, `services`, `forward_reservations`; `tools/hcal_readout/config.json` carrier/module/electronics/services objects, all at the assigned revision. No additional public-source claims or new references were needed. No engineering, radiation, sustained-rate or physics sign-off is granted.

**HCAL-20261015-SysArch — read-only interface assessment**

Reviewed nODD revision **`5b4e5d9e563505aea17e9b792458708c3175ec4a`**. Historical LAr checkout independently verified at **`72d37ee9a56182e4ba974791a848a738c19cf092`**. No files changed; no native runtime, field, structural or thermal calculation performed.

The selected SiW layout has a credible HCAL technology direction, but its current HCAL envelope is ahead of its implemented hardware. The old cassette and assembly prototypes provide useful component evidence; they do **not** validate the enlarged, service-constrained HCAL now drawn in LAYOUT-001.

### Findings and evidence

**1. Three different objects must remain distinguishable.**

- The retained ODD comparison uses 36 repetitions of **30 mm Steel235 + 16 mm siPCBMix + 3 mm scintillator + 2 mm Air**: 1.836 m total. The PCB proxy contributes 576 mm over the stack; its recorded areal mass is 290.924 g/cm², including 238.198 g/cm² copper. Removing that material changes shower depth/material as well as packaging. It cannot be described as a geometry refactor. Source: `5b4e5d9:docs/design/DES-027-calorimeter-description-assessment.md:100–122`, referring to ODD `c167363f3d4ad1540a577af99071283caf54f3a6`.
- DES028/029 replace the unexplained PCB bulk with physical tile/readout/cooling components. HCAL pitch becomes **41.275 mm**, comprising 30 mm absorber, 10.275 mm cassette and 1 mm installation gap; 36 layers give 1.4859 m sampling/package depth, plus 10 mm back cover. These are unsigned prototype choices. Sources: `tools/calorimeter_hardware/cassettes.json`, HCAL object; `tools/calorimeter_hardware/assembly.py:24–27`; `DES-028:24–36,48–63`.
- Current **LAYOUT-001** moves this **1.4959 m outline**, without regenerating detailed HCAL hardware, to barrel apothems **2.600–4.0959 m**, half-length **4.4832 m**, and endcaps **|z|=4.8832–6.3791 m**, inner/outer apothems **0.300/4.0859 m**. Maximum barrel corner radius is **4.176143 m**. Source: `DES-034-siw-service-envelopes.md:36–58,148–152`; `tools/siw_services/study.py:37–43,117–122`.

The current layout page explicitly calls HCAL an outline and identifies FCal and muon systems as absent (`docs/layouts/LAYOUT-001-tracker-3t-siw.md:16–26`). Do not carry DES029 mass, channel, overlap or acceptance results onto the current outline.

**2. The existing HCAL assembly demonstrates construction consistency and also demonstrates unacceptable packing loss.**

The executed DES029 fixture contains 27,200 barrel and 9,216 endcap HCAL cassettes. Recorded HCAL mass is approximately **2,099.816 t**, and active plate-area fractions are **52.9–78.3% in the barrel and 38.8% in endcaps**. These totals belong to the smaller historical geometry (`DES-029-calorimeter-assemblies.md:87–104`).

Its native audit records zero overlaps at 10 nm and independent mass/shape checks. However, sampled `|eta|≥2.4` directions cross absorber without active elements; sparse Geant4 checks use three muons, zero field and selected cassettes. This is not hadron containment evidence (`docs/validation/DES-029/results.md`, “57 native ROOT material rays” and “Geant4 sparse-sector saved-hit audit”).

The defect follows directly from the packer: width must fit inside the narrow sector face, with 40 mm edge allocations; `floor` then selects whole 400×380 mm cassettes (`assembly.py:45–70`). Recorded first HCAL sensitive radius is **1.48315 m**, despite a 300 mm nominal aperture. Source: `DES-029-endcap-coverage-repair.md`, “Where the reported area goes”; `docs/validation/DES-029/endcap-coverage-review.json`, HCAL baseline. Replication or staggering alone cannot repair that large inner hole.

**3. ECAL service feasibility does not yet include HCAL services.**

DES034 reserves the circular **R=2.300–2.600 m** backbone and **400 mm rear break** to route ECAL services outward to **R=4.300 m**. Its input heat, powered-interface counts and pipe counts are exclusively ECAL (`tools/siw_services/inputs.json:source_facts`; `study.py:47–78`).

The independently reproduced lane checks therefore establish no demonstrated spare capacity for HCAL LV/bias, data, calibration, cooling, collection manifolds or mechanical attachments. This matters because the old HCAL cassette population alone implies approximately **110.63 kW local heat and 5.293 kg/s ideal water flow** under DES028 hypotheses. Those values are scale indicators, not current HCAL totals.

The local prototype has useful face ports and flush tube ends, but real connectors, seals, bends, collector networks and circuit closure are unqualified (`DES029:62–69`). DES034 also states that existing ECAL tubes stop inside plates and local connections remain absent (`DES034:36–41,98–104`). Both subsystems need a connected service graph and an aggregate capacity budget before accepting this annulus.

**4. Depth is preserved nominally, but transition and forward containment are unresolved.**

I independently evaluated straight IP rays using the retained DES034 allocation and `r=z/sinh|eta|`. At sector centre:

- Full traversal of the **barrel outline’s radial thickness** is possible only below approximately `|eta|=0.9467`; any barrel-outline intersection ends at `1.3131`.
- Endcap-outline intersection begins at approximately `1.0129`; full axial traversal with radial containment begins at `1.2283`.

These are analytic outline bounds, **not active-layer or containment results**. They identify a transition requiring explicit combined barrel/endcap sampling and services studies. The 400 mm service break cannot be accepted from envelope clearance alone.

Forward implications are sharper:

- An `eta=4` ray stays inside the HCAL’s 300 mm aperture: the empty FCal reservation gives radii **166.11–233.75 mm**.
- At `eta=5`, that reservation’s front/back ray radii are **61.09/85.97 mm**. Its 80 mm inner radius permits only **0.442843 m axial intersection near the rear**, out of the 1.8459 m reserved length.
- At `eta=5.2`, the ray misses the reservation entirely.

Thus the reservation’s documented `eta=4` accommodation cannot establish the earlier human-directed calorimetry investigation to `|eta|<5` (`ADR-006-global-envelope-and-field-hypotheses.md`, “Context and review direction”). It contains no hardware anyway. Beam pipe beyond 4 m, shielding, machine aperture, support and services remain unresolved (`DES034:124–137`).

**5. Steel is a detector-wide magnetic and structural interface.**

The source gives a transport composition, not a qualified steel grade or magnetic constitutive law: `cassettes.json:steel_recipe` is Fe 0.998/C 0.002. DES029 provides aluminium rails/flanges/rims/back covers, while joint design, deflection, handling, lifting and seismic support are explicitly unqualified (`DES029:42–50`).

The enlarged DES034 HCAL outline volume is **1.240875914×** the previous outline. That is not a mass or support scaling law (`study.py:105–111,132–133`; retained allocations). Neither the current field nor force/load paths are established.

Primary public evidence reinforces the need for this gate:

- The [CMS force study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02793v1), abstract, calculates absorber forces even for low-permeability stainless steel.
- The [CMS construction account]([external URL redacted; see source journal]), structural and assembly paragraphs, describes connected absorber plates, a backflange, dedicated supports and a physical deformation test against FEA.

These are hardware categories and validation precedents; their dated configurations and numerical dimensions should not be imported into nODD.

### Interface register recommended for the next HCAL design

| Interface and endpoint owners | Contract to resolve | Review evidence |
|---|---|---|
| ECAL ↔ HCAL ↔ common services | Polygon apothems versus circular corridor radii; local collectors, bends and service exits; ECAL plus HCAL concurrent loads | Joint 3D routing, corner and adverse-capacity checks; material ledger and circuit connectivity |
| HCAL absorber/support ↔ magnet system | Certified grade or bracketed B–H/permeability; steel’s role in return flux; forces and attachment reactions | Installed nonlinear field/energy/force solution and owned load paths; apply existing magnetic sizing policy |
| HCAL barrel ↔ endcaps | Sampling topology through axial break, rails, seams and service trunks; installation/opening sequence | Layer-by-layer signed eta/phi masks, interaction-length/dead-material maps and hadron leakage studies |
| HCAL endcaps ↔ FCal/interaction region | Aperture at every depth, technology handover, beam pipe, shielding and routing | Agreed coverage/depth definition, finite-volume material and active-crossing scans, machine-interface review |
| HCAL ↔ muon system/global supports | Punch-through absorber role, outer corner envelope, feet/bearings and access | Common envelope and load register; transport/background study before allocating additional iron |
| Physical HCAL ↔ software/readout | Barrel local `(tangent, axial, outward)`; endcap `(tangent, radial, outward)`; proper negative-end rotation; physical IDs separate from cells | Native transforms, bounded identifier ranges and saved-hit checks, following DES029 conventions |

### Proposed review gates following the ECAL method

1. **Operating and interface gate:** agree the hadron-collider radiation/rate/lifetime regions, continuous power, temperature and coverage contracts; retain steel/scintillator as the human-preferred starting technology. Assign both endpoints of every boundary above. No new numerical requirements are selected here.
2. **Tile/board gate:** qualify a sourced tile, SiPM, readout and cooling package against those conditions; reconcile the component ledger with the removed ODD mixture. Preserve the comparison configuration.
3. **Inner endcap carrier gate:** design this before full repetition. Compare smaller tile-board families, inner/edge strips and broader carriers with peripheral shared services. Physical tile manufacturing, optical isolation, board margins and support remain explicit. This follows the existing ECAL repair approach without copying silicon-specific edge-sensor solutions.
4. **Barrel and complete-layer gate:** demonstrate connected services, support/load paths, realistic seams, assembly/replacement access and material conservation. Publish active masks and useful sampling versus eta/phi.
5. **Integrated feasibility gate:** regenerate HCAL for the selected DES034 boundaries; recompute mass, channels, power, coolant, steel/field effects and support reactions. Then repeat native overlap/ID/material checks and carry out combined hadron containment/leakage and transition studies with independently reviewed response assumptions.

Historical **LAYOUT-002/LAr** is useful only as a documented alternative demonstrating how cryostats, access and services propagate into HCAL size: its HCAL outline is 3.130–4.6259 m with half-length 5.860 m and endcaps 6.360–7.8559 m (`72d37ee:DES-033-allegro-lar-endcaps.md:35–60`). It is absent from current main and should not be presented as a current candidate or used to import a cryostat into the warm HCAL.

**Checks actually run:** exact-revision `git show` inspection of assigned and supporting sources; branch/HEAD/status checks; historical LAr revision verification; `python3 -B tools/siw_services/study.py --check` **PASS**; its **10 unit controls PASS**; independent standard-library ray/outline arithmetic above. No runtime setup was needed. The coordinator should retain this contribution and actual checks in the task session record; no sign-off or acceptance is implied.

The coordinator’s proposed **1,558 mm depth amendment**, full-face/quadrant endcap packing and 33-row staggered barrel are coherent prototype directions. They need the following common contracts in both PRs.

### Depth and common envelope

DES036 fixes the carrier at **380×240×12 mm**. Retaining 36 layers, 30 mm steel, 1 mm installation and a 10 mm back cover requires:

\[
36(30+12+1)+10=1558\ \mathrm{mm}.
\]

This exceeds DES034’s 1,495.9 mm allocation by **62.1 mm**. Even zero installation gaps require 1,522 mm. Source: `tools/hcal_readout/config.json`, `carrier.size_mm/absorber_mm`; `DES-036`, “Shared carrier”; `DES-034`, “External backbone and HCAL interfaces”.

Recommend the **explicit proposed outline amendment**:

- Barrel: front apothem **2,600 mm**, outer apothem **4,158 mm**, half-length **4,483.2 mm**.
- Endcaps: front **|z|=4,883.2 mm**, back **6,441.2 mm**, inner/outer apothems **300/4,148 mm**.
- Preserve ECAL’s circular **R=2,300–2,600 mm** annulus and **400 mm** rear egress break.
- Leave the existing empty FCal reservation unchanged, as instructed.

These are proposed changes, not already approved detector dimensions. Retain DES034 as the comparison.

Reducing layer count or installation clearance is a separate physical alternative:

| Layers / installation | Depth including 10 mm cover | Difference from old allocation |
|---|---:|---:|
| 36 / 1 mm | 1,558 mm | +62.1 mm |
| 36 / 0.5 mm | 1,540 mm | +44.1 mm |
| 35 / 1 mm | 1,515 mm | +19.1 mm |
| 35 / 0.5 mm | 1,497.5 mm | +1.6 mm |
| 34 / 1 mm | 1,472 mm | −23.9 mm |

The amendment preserves the sampling comparison and unchanged module. It leaves **no additional radial/axial depth budget beyond the named 10 mm cover**. Frames and collectors therefore require explicit lateral/axial allocations or further amendments.

The amended barrel corner is **4,239.460 mm**, rather than 4,158 mm. DES034’s R=4,300 mm egress, less its 25 mm water-jacket radius and 20 mm clearance, leaves only **15.540 mm extra clearance**. This passes that particular analytic inequality; it demonstrates no additional HCAL service capacity.

### Barrel organization and phase constraints

Use common carrier local axes:

\[
(x,y,z)=(e_\phi,e_z,e_r).
\]

Thus tubes run axially and the shared connector bay points toward local +y.

With **33 rows**, 240 mm carrier length and proposed **20 mm inter-row collector strips**, occupied length is:

\[
33(240)+32(20)=8560\ \mathrm{mm}.
\]

Keeping 20 mm end flanges inside the half-length gives usable bounds ±4,463.2 mm. A centred row pattern ends at ±4,280 mm; therefore each layer’s axial phase must satisfy:

\[
|s_\ell|\le183.2\ \mathrm{mm}.
\]

The proposed **−60, 0, +60 mm** phases leave at least **123.2 mm** between carrier extrema and flange inner faces.

DES036’s active core field spans local y **−101.85 to +77.85 mm**. At 260 mm row pitch, aligned rows produce **80.3 mm macro gaps** between core fields. The gap intervals for the three proposed phases have no common intersection, giving a useful geometric reason for staggering. Physical tile gaps, tangential seams and edge losses still require complete core checks.

With 33 rows, phase zero places a carrier across the midplane. An “aligned midplane-zero” control therefore needs a different phase: **+130 mm** is admissible, leaves **53.2 mm** minimum flange clearance, and places the nominal core gap at **z=−52.15 to +28.15 mm**. Report its asymmetric end reserves. An aligned phase-zero control remains useful for correlated cracks away from the midplane.

For tangential packing, evaluate the full rectangular carrier against the **narrowest radial face**, rather than the layer midpoint or outer face:

\[
|x_c|+\frac{380}{2}
\le r_{\rm carrier,front}\tan(\pi/16)-\text{named edge allowance}.
\]

Check all carrier corners and every layer. Keep the proposed 1 mm tangential gap, sector edge rails and any staggering offsets explicit.

### Endcap organization and frames

Full-face Cartesian packing within mechanical quadrants avoids the earlier artificial 16-wedge packing hole. Keep **mechanical quadrants independent of 16 readout-sector IDs**, with deterministic ID assignment documented for carriers spanning a readout boundary.

The failure being avoided is substantial:

- A 380 mm tangential carrier in a 16-sector wedge needs an inner radius of at least **955.195 mm**, even with zero additional edge allowance.
- Rotating it to 240 mm tangential width still needs **603.281 mm**.
- Neither reaches the nominal 300 mm aperture.

These are lower bounds, not selected active apertures. Source: DES036 carrier dimensions and the wedge-width relationship documented in `DES-029-endcap-coverage-repair.md`, “Where the reported area goes”.

Do not clip carriers, boards or tiles at aperture/quadrant boundaries. Reject an intersecting carrier and report the resulting uncovered region. Whole-face packing must respect the inner aperture and outer polygon at **every corner**, including rotated carriers.

Specify signed frame vectors. For example:

- Unrotated positive-end carrier: **`(−e_phi, +e_r, +e_z)`**, determinant +1.
- Rotated positive-end carrier: **`(+e_r, +e_phi, +e_z)`**, determinant +1.

The unsigned description “tangent/radial/outward” is ambiguous: `(+e_phi,+e_r,+e_z)` has determinant −1. Generate the negative end through a proper 180° rotation of the entire positive-end arrangement. Transform cooling ports, connector bay, normals and IDs together.

Unchanged DES036 hardware has a nominal core-face ceiling of approximately **69.64%**, from `72×29.7²/(380×240)`, before packing losses. Report face fractions and directional sampling separately; do not promise near-continuous active area from improved packing alone.

### Cross-PR physical and service invariants

| Interface / owners | Required invariant |
|---|---|
| Common module ↔ barrel/endcap | Retain exact DES036 source/config hashes, materials, 12 mm depth, ports, connectors and channel accounting. Repetition adds placements, not another copy of shared hardware. |
| Absorber ↔ carrier | Assembly owns each steel plate exactly once. Omit the removable DES036 reference patch from all repetitions. Supports receive separate material/load ownership. |
| Carrier ↔ row collector | Four transformed cooling handoffs per carrier; two through-flow branches. Connector bay requires mating/access space on local +y. A 20 mm strip is a proposed reservation, not qualified plumbing. |
| Collector ↔ sector/quadrant trunk | Name actual passages and displacement of frames/rails. A material-filled edge rail cannot also be an empty trunk. Cross-steel routing requires modeled cuts and structural assessment. |
| HCAL ↔ ECAL/common services | Preserve the ECAL annulus and rear egress. HCAL flows, cables and supports require their own capacity/material allocation; DES034 budgets ECAL loads. |
| HCAL ↔ global supports/magnets | Plate → rails/frame → flange/bearing load paths must be named. Include absorber/support steel in the installed field/force problem; transport composition is not B–H data or a structural qualification. |
| Endcaps ↔ beam/FCal | Preserve the 300 mm bore and existing FCal reservation. Keep downstream pipe, shielding and forward coverage unresolved; packing changes do not establish forward hadron depth. |

The design PRs can retain explicitly empty reservations. They must distinguish those from implemented pipes, cables and manifolds, and cannot claim a connected network until every internal endpoint has an owned connection or declared external handoff.

### Barrel/endcap transition

For the amended outline, straight IP sector-centre bounds give:

- Any barrel intersection: `|eta|≤1.31308`.
- Any endcap intersection: `|eta|≥1.00132`.
- Complete barrel radial traversal ends at approximately **0.93561**.
- Complete endcap axial traversal begins at approximately **1.22372**.

The outline intersection ranges overlap; the 400 mm break does **not** create an angular interval with zero HCAL-outline intersection. However, directions approximately **0.94–1.22** traverse partial regions and the service transition. Overlapping envelopes establish neither useful sampling nor containment. Require actual core crossings, steel/dead-material paths and subsequent shower leakage studies across approximately eta 0.9–1.4, including seam phi controls.

**Actual checks:** exact-revision source inspection; independent standard-library depth, corner, wedge-fit, axial-phase and IP-ray arithmetic. No native geometry, service routing, structural, thermal, magnetic or performance check was run. All proposed dimensions remain subject to human review.

Assignment **HCAL-20261015-PhysVal** completed read-only against nODD commit **`5b4e5d9e563505aea17e9b792458708c3175ec4a`**. I assessed the pinned baseline and primary literature independently; I have not reviewed the coordinator’s eventual report.

**Conclusion:** steel/scintillator is an appropriate candidate for a hadron collider. The current evidence does **not** establish that ODD’s particular sampling recipe, nODD’s present packaging, or its readout and operating assumptions constitute a feasible pp HCAL. The strongest present conclusions concern geometry and material bookkeeping. Containment, high-rate operation, aging and reconstructed performance remain open.

### Evidence boundary

Examined at the assigned commit:

- `docs/design/DES-027-calorimeter-description-assessment.md`
- `docs/design/DES-028-calorimeter-cassettes.md`
- `docs/design/DES-029-calorimeter-assemblies.md`
- `docs/layouts/README.md`
- `reference/manifest.yaml`, including its ODD and CALICE records
- `docs/validation/DES-027/odd-inventory.json`
- `docs/validation/DES-028/results.md`
- `docs/validation/DES-029/results.md`, `native.json`, `transport.json`
- `docs/decisions/ADR-001-upstream-baseline.md` and `ADR-003-validation-and-artifact-policy.md`

The recorded ODD comparison revision is **`c167363f3d4ad1540a577af99071283caf54f3a6`**. DES027 also establishes equality of the two calorimeter sampling XML files with ODD v6.0.2 at **`d70556f33b1c36abdf101a07ad8cf57eb56fbdf1`**; that does not establish whole-detector equality.

The working tree contained the coordinator’s two untracked `SESSION-2026-10-15-hcal-realism` log files. I did not use those as target evidence or modify any files.

The old DES029 native execution identifies **`9b409b71eb2cfa0b4df1cd9fcd15ff5058b8f3a1`**, `dirty: true`, with separate compact, factory, library and validator hashes. Its results are retained execution evidence, not a clean-commit-only reproduction claim.

### Findings and implications

**High — the material correction changes the calorimeter’s physics.**  
ODD has 36 repeats of 30 mm steel, 16 mm copper-rich PCB mixture, 3 mm scintillator and 2 mm air. Replacing the unsupported PCB proxy is justified engineering work, but preserving the steel and scintillator thicknesses does not preserve hadronic depth or sampling response.

From the pinned inventory, the PCB allocation contains **238.198 g/cm² of copper** along the normal column. Dividing by the PDG copper nuclear interaction length, **137.3 g/cm²**, gives approximately **1.735 interaction lengths associated with that copper mass alone**. Similarly, 108 cm of pure iron corresponds to approximately **6.440 nuclear interaction lengths** using the PDG iron value of 16.77 cm. These are elemental screening proxies, not calculated Steel235 or complete-mixture depths. They make clear that the change needs fresh native interaction-length scans and shower-leakage studies. [PDG copper, nuclear interaction-length row](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/AtomicNuclearProperties/HTML/copper_Cu.html), [PDG iron, nuclear interaction-length row](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2026/AtomicNuclearProperties/HTML/iron_Fe.html).

**High — the existing assembly has a known acceptance defect.**  
DES029 reports HCAL active plate-area fractions of 52.9–78.3% in barrel layers and 38.8% in the two endcaps. Its sparse native angular scan finds no active crossings at the sampled φ values for |η| ≥ 2.4 despite absorber traversal. These facts justify redesign of packing and boundaries; they do not quantify full shower inefficiency. The scan is too sparse to establish the complete η–φ loss map.

**High — a geometry PASS is being correctly bounded, and that boundary must remain.**  
DES029 retains zero native overlaps, checked placement/mass inventories and 384 sampled inherited-ID round trips. Its transport evidence comprises **three seeded 10 GeV μ− events** in sparse selected-cassette fixtures, FTFP_BERT, zero field. This supports hit hierarchy and identifier checks. It does not establish hadronic response, optical response, SiPM behavior, pileup rejection, complete-detector transport or jets/MET performance.

**High — the operating point is still a hypothesis.**  
DES028’s 20 °C water-cooled HCAL, 55 V bias, 2 μA/channel dark current and 5 mW/channel continuous electronics budget are explicitly project hypotheses. They cannot establish end-of-life temperature, dark noise, MIP efficiency, sustained data capacity or thermal stability. DES029’s 110.64 kW HCAL heat total is an inference from those hypotheses and installed counts, not a measured cooling requirement.

**High — “current” requires three separately named configurations.**

1. The pinned upstream ODD comparison.
2. The isolated DES028/029 hardware prototypes.
3. The selected layout, whose HCAL is currently a service-constrained outline according to the pinned layout README.

Mixing their envelopes, coverage, mass or validation states would create a detector configuration that has not been examined.

### What primary hardware evidence supports

**Steel/scintillator as a hadron-collider technology: strong support, with location-dependent qualification.**  
The ATLAS Run-2 paper documents a working steel/scintillator calorimeter in pp collisions, with WLS-fibre/PMT readout covering |η| < 1.7. Its architecture differs materially from embedded SiPM-on-tile electronics. Sections 7.3–7.4 show that timing and noise depend on pileup; neighboring bunch crossings contribute when the electrical pulse extends beyond bunch spacing. These are concrete reasons to validate waveforms and reconstruction, not just timestamp resolution. [ATLAS, arXiv:2401.16034v2, §§2, 7.3–7.4](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.16034v2).

**CALICE supports the active-element concept, but not direct reuse of its pp operating assumptions.**  
The technological prototype uses 30 mm tiles and SiPMs with 2668 pixels. Its design discussion explicitly connects low average power to linear-collider trains and long quiet gaps. SPIROC2E uses 50 ns shaping and 16 analog-memory cells; filling the memory triggers a change from acquisition to readout. Its approximately 0.68 ns single-channel result uses the fast-clock test mode. None of these facts establishes continuous high-rate pp suitability. [CALICE, arXiv:2209.15327v1, §§2.1–2.3.1, 6.4](https://arxiv.org/html/2209.15327v1).

**Modern HGCAL work is a useful pp integration precedent.**  
Fabian Hummer’s October 2025 contribution describes silicon in high-radiation/pileup regions and scintillator/SiPMs in outer endcap regions. Its validation slice uses five tile modules, a motherboard and a copper cooling plate, with tests of clocks, commands, counter synchronization and combined silicon/scintillator readout. This is a good model for a bounded nODD cassette-to-readout demonstration. The inspected source is the conference summary; I do not claim review of the later 2026 proceedings PDF, which returned a bot challenge. [TWEPP 2025, contribution 6554663, summary]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).

**There is now direct SiPM-on-tile pp operating evidence, but at substantially different conditions.**  
The RHIC prototype paper reports room-temperature parasitic operation during 200 GeV pp running in 2024 and an estimated fluence around 10¹⁰ 1-MeV neq/cm². Its standalone trigger/readout and limited readout population do not demonstrate an HL-LHC-scale continuously read-out detector. It is useful evidence for deployment, MIP calibration and radiation monitoring. [Zhang et al., arXiv:2501.08586v1, §§2–5](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.08586v1).

**Scintillator lifetime cannot be reduced to accumulated dose alone.**  
CMS measurements find larger light-output damage at lower dose rate for a fixed dose within the measured range; their conclusions warn that damage fits depend on materials, geometry and environment and that new tile systems need dose-rate studies. This rules out adopting a generic “polystyrene survives X Gy” number as an nODD lifetime qualification. [CMS, arXiv:2001.06553v2, §§6–7; HTML headings 0.6–0.7](https://arxiv.org/html/2001.06553v2). The later ATLAS optics study independently treats dose-rate effects and separates measured Run-2 behavior from HL-LHC extrapolation. [ATLAS, arXiv:2412.15944v2, §5.4](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.15944v2).

### Invalid extrapolations to exclude

- **CALICE resolution → nODD resolution.** The frequently cited stochastic improvement from about 58%/√E to 45%/√E concerns selected 10–80 GeV pion samples. That apparatus used a different active stack and included a tail catcher. Early shower-start selection suppresses leakage. The paper’s fixed e/π correction is a calibration convention for that study, not a universal material e/h ratio. [CALICE, arXiv:1207.4210v2, §§2.1–2.3, 4](https://arxiv.org/html/1207.4210v2).
- **Thirty-millimeter tiles → optimal pp granularity.** Their suitability must be re-evaluated against pp cell occupancy, shower density, channel count, saturation and reconstruction confusion.
- **Subnanosecond single-hit timing → equivalent shower or pileup timing.** Threshold, energy, time walk, photon statistics, clock distribution and delayed hadronic activity matter.
- **Room-temperature unirradiated noise → end-of-life noise.** Temperature, fluence and dark-current evolution must be propagated together.
- **More realistic passive material → automatically better response.** Removing copper changes containment; adding actual gaps introduces losses previously absent.
- **Particle flow → immunity to HCAL defects.** Charged-particle measurements can benefit from tracking, while neutral hadrons, cracks, overlap confusion and MET tails still require calorimeter validation.

The shower-time literature also shows delayed neutron-related components extending beyond prompt deposits; both absorber and active medium affect them. Consequently, narrowing integration windows needs a measured bias-versus-pileup tradeoff. [CALICE T3B, arXiv:1404.6454v2, §§1–2, 6.4](https://arxiv.org/html/1404.6454v2).

### Proposed requirements-to-observables matrix

These are **proposed validation gates**, not accepted numerical requirements. Numerical tolerances must be set before interpreting acceptance, as required by ADR003.

| Requirement/question | Observable and necessary comparison | Gate before a suitability claim |
|---|---|---|
| Appropriate collider operating point | √s, bunch spacing, bunch pattern, pileup distribution, luminosity profile, lifetime, maximum energies and η coverage | Publish one operating contract; keep alternatives separately labeled |
| Adequate depth and containment | Directional X₀/λI; shower profiles; rear/side leakage; full energy-response distributions and low-response tails versus energy/η/φ | Compare original ODD, explicit cassette stack and candidate depth options using a declared leakage-accounting convention |
| Stable noncompensating response | Electron and pion response, species dependence, response nonlinearity; core resolution **and** tails | Establish raw and calibrated response separately; validate software compensation on held-out energies/configurations |
| Pileup resilience | In-time and out-of-time cell energy/noise, occupancy, bunch assignment, baseline shifts and reconstruction bias | Overlay the required neighboring crossings through the actual pulse/integration model; include bunch-train edges |
| Useful timing | Hit/shower timing bias, resolution and non-Gaussian tails versus deposited energy, thresholds, position and aging | Demonstrate the timing working point together with its lost-energy and pileup tradeoffs |
| Radiation lifetime | Position-dependent dose, dose rate, neutron fluence/spectrum and electronics exposure; residual light yield, dark current and noise | Map exposure onto selected tile/SiPM/ASIC evidence; evaluate beginning and end of life with uncertainty |
| Adequate dynamic range | Photoelectron and fired-pixel distributions, recovery/occupancy, saturation fraction, ADC clipping and correction residuals | Test dense shower cores plus pileup; establish maximum usable cell signal and EOL MIP efficiency |
| Calibratability | Pedestals, gain, temperature coefficient, MIP scale, gain-range intercalibration, timing offsets and monitoring reach | Specify calibration hardware and constants; distinguish LED gain monitoring from scintillator light-yield monitoring |
| Acceptable cracks/services | Fine η–φ maps of passive depth and sensitive crossings; response/tail scans across seams, aperture and barrel–endcap transition | Remove unexplained blind corridors; quantify remaining losses with showers, vertices and tolerances |
| Sustained feasible readout | Buffer occupancy, dead time, trigger/data bandwidth, link load, error rates, heat/current versus activity | Exercise a continuously powered cassette/readout slice with a sourced architecture |
| Credible jets and MET | Calorimeter-only and PF jet scale/resolution; neutral response; dijet/γ+jet balance; MET components, resolution and tails | Use complete ECAL–HCAL/passive geometry and named reconstruction, pileup and calibration configurations |
| Robustness to failures | Response to masked channels, failed boards, cooling/power groups and service dead zones | Demonstrate degradation behavior and maintainability assumptions before full-system qualification |

For response, define at least \(R=E_\text{reco}/E_\text{true}\), its mean or median, a declared core-width metric and full-tail probabilities using thresholds agreed in advance. A Gaussian core fit alone can conceal precisely the leakage and crack effects relevant to pp MET.

### Suggested staged programme

1. **Operating and material contract.** Resolve machine scenarios, lifetime and response scope; retain the old copper-rich model as a named comparison. Specify which current prototype hypotheses need supplier, irradiation or system evidence.
2. **One qualified response tile/cassette model.** Add sourced scintillation/quenching, spatial light collection, photoelectron statistics, SiPM recovery/saturation/noise, pulse shape, thresholds, calibration and aging. A measured parameterization is sufficient where full optical-photon simulation adds little.
3. **A fully populated stack.** Preserve the existing component hierarchy but replace sparse muon demonstrations with shower samples. Include ECAL and upstream passive material, boundary scans, rear leakage instrumentation in the validation fixture and at least one justified hadronic-model cross-check.
4. **Continuous-operation slice.** Follow the modern HGCAL style of sensor-to-backend validation with a realistic cooling and grounding environment. Compare embedded and remote electronics where their heat/material/service costs materially differ.
5. **Sector/endcap repair and integration.** Prove active coverage, service routing, installed material and dead-region response before promoting the current HCAL outline to a complete detector candidate.
6. **Jets/MET and independent review.** Freeze benchmark definitions, train/calibrate on separate samples, retain adverse tails, and request human subsystem/performance review. If the 36 × 30 mm absorber comparison fails containment requirements, propose a reviewed depth/tail-catcher amendment; do not compensate by silently retuning response.

For comparisons, change geometry, digitization and reconstruction in separately controlled steps. Propagate material, response, calibration, irradiation, shower-model and event-generator uncertainties explicitly. A physics-list spread is a model comparison, not automatically a confidence interval.

**Actual checks performed:** pinned Git source/report inspection, dirty-state inspection, primary-source reading and arithmetic reproduction of the two elemental interaction-length screening estimates. **No DD4hep/Geant4 runtime, shower simulation, thermal test or reconstruction validation was performed. No files changed and no sign-off granted.**

**Recommendation:** no scientific blocker to starting this isolated nominal module. Its planning scenarios, channel ownership and qualification boundaries are adequately distinguished from established requirements and measured performance. One concrete tolerance limitation should be recorded before claiming that the candidate package fits over its specified dimensional range.

**P2 — nominal package fit does not cover the sourced height tolerance.**  
DES036 lines 44–45 place the SiPM front at z = 2.70 mm and the recess front at 2.60 mm: 0.10 mm nominal clearance. The cited package height is 0.85 ± 0.15 mm. Holding its rear/solder reference plane fixed, maximum height moves the front to 2.55 mm, intruding 0.05 mm beyond the current recess. The datasheet also assigns ±0.15 mm to the nominal 0.26 mm chip-to-package centre offset.

Action: explicitly label the present geometry as nominal-only, or enlarge/reposition the recess using a declared tolerance allowance. Include height and active-centre tolerances in subsequent coupling/assembly studies. This does not invalidate nominal prototype construction. Evidence: DES036 lines 24, 32, 44–45; Hamamatsu **KAPD1070E05, June 2025, PDF5, drawing KAPDA0205EB**. [Manufacturer datasheet]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).

**Arithmetic independently checked**

| Quantity | Result |
|---|---:|
| Ordinary inputs per chip | 72 |
| Connected ordinary inputs per module | 36 |
| Powered channels per carrier, including auxiliaries | 156 for 72 tiles |
| Assumed event payload per chip | 2,560 bits |
| Usable DAQ capacity per chip | 2.048 Gbit/s |
| Utilization at 750 kHz | **93.75%** |
| Utilization at 1 MHz | **125%** |
| Ideal latency margin | **12 samples / 300 ns** |
| Carrier heat at 2 μA/SiPM | **5.939381 W** |
| Carrier heat at 100 μA/SiPM | **6.235733 W** |
| Carrier heat at 1 mA/SiPM | **8.957333 W** |
| Corresponding ideal water flows at 5 K rise | **0.284181 / 0.298360 / 0.428581 g/s** |

These reproduce the stated formulas, including LV conversion loss. They exclude the explicitly deferred bias-regulation loss.

The 750 kHz case has only **6.25% remaining capacity under the assumed payload model**. Preserve the term *bandwidth screen*: padding all channels is conservative in channel occupancy, but does not prove the complete packet format, retransmission policy, trigger-output bandwidth, carrier export capacity or burst/dead-time behavior. The document already states the essential limitations at line 70; retain them in generated tables and any PASS labels.

**Claims assessed as consistent**

- **Operating direction:** 14 TeV is established. ADR006 additionally records the earlier HL-LHC study direction and calorimetry toward |η| < 5. DES036 correctly treats 25 ns sampling, 750 kHz/1 MHz acceptance and 12.5 μs latency as explicit planning choices rather than consequences of collision energy. No correction to those distinctions is required.
- **Channels and power:** 78 powered channels versus 72 ordinary sensor inputs is handled correctly. The 36 unused ordinary inputs are not silently reused or assumed free of power.
- **Electronics precedent:** the inspected 2026 HGCROC paper supports the 512-entry circular latency buffer, 32-entry output FIFO, continuous bunch-crossing trigger path and below-15 mW/channel requirement. It does not supply a qualified nODD package, power measurement or tile timing result. DES036 states this accurately. The source also distinguishes production subversions and their SEE behavior; a future component selection should name its exact version. [Bouyjou et al., JINST 21 (2026) C01016, §1/PDF2 and §§3.1–3.2/PDF5–6]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).
- **SiPM reference:** the manufacturer confirms the stated active area, pixel count and nominal breakdown/overvoltage framework. The 42 V value is correctly presented as a starting bias requiring device-specific adjustment, rather than a guaranteed operating voltage for every delivered device.
- **Material proxy:** distinguishing undoped C8H8 transport material from a selected scintillator formulation and optical response is scientifically sound. Preserve that distinction in sensitive-hit output interpretation.
- **Stress currents:** 100 μA and 1 mA/device are useful conditional heat inputs. They are correctly not called end-of-life predictions. They do not establish dark-count noise, photon detection efficiency, MIP separation or self-heating stability.
- **Forward applicability:** DES035 appropriately retains regional qualification and a separate forward design. Add a short cross-reference in DES036’s operating scope if the module is later described as “common” across regions; common hardware does not establish uniform environmental suitability.
- **Native/smoke boundaries:** lines 76–78 correctly restrict geometry, identifier and seeded-muon checks. Such checks cannot establish optical coupling, shower response, saturation, radiation survival, sustained acquisition, thermal performance or full HCAL feasibility.

**Next scientific gate:** retain these conditional budgets while constructing the nominal module; then validate tile light collection/MIP response, SiPM/front-end matching and continuous acquisition under explicit noise, activity and temperature scenarios. Keep continuously sampled trigger information distinct from triggered DAQ export.

This is a technical recommendation for the isolated prototype, not engineering sign-off or detector acceptance.
